blocks.text: Lots and land in Heritage Woods
What trades here

items.t: What land actually consists of here: the OCP describes the Heritage Mountain grouping, including Heritage Woods, as a mix of single detached homes and townhouses plus a small number of apartment units, with small-scale multi-unit housing expected to add gentle density over time. Detached homes are freehold; townhouses are strata titled. Minimum lot sizes are set zone by zone in Zoning Bylaw No. 2937.
No named fee-simple bare-land subdivision offered as vacant lots is verified for this area.

They are built townhouse stock, named here only so a land reader does not mistake them for lot inventory. The OCP's "small number of apartment units" is a grouping-level land-use description for the whole Heritage Mountain grouping, not a named Heritage Woods building.

Hillside character — the diligence that decides buildable area: lots with a watercourse need a riparian assessment and Zoning Bylaw Section 5.4 setbacks, and environmentally sensitive and steep-slope development permit areas can apply on this hillside. No floodplain or ALR land was confirmed in Heritage Woods — there is no ALR split to state for this area.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Heritage Woods

items.t: Heritage Woods is a hillside neighbourhood on Port Moody's north shore — the eastern part of the Heritage Mountain grouping in the Official Community Plan, below Anmore and beside the Coquitlam border. David Avenue connects Heritage Woods west into Port Moody and east into Coquitlam; Heritage Mountain Boulevard connects south toward Ioco Road.
Nearby areas: Heritage Mountain and Mountain Meadows to the west, North Shore Pt Moody below, Anmore to the north, Coquitlam (Westwood Plateau side) to the east.

Port Moody community, September 2026 — detached: median $1,685,000, $608/sq ft, 96% sale-to-list, 33 days; Condos & Townhomes: median $715,000, $666/sq ft, 94% sale-to-list, 29 days. (SnapStats, September 2026)
Schools (SD43; Ministry-listed names only): Heritage Woods Secondary School at 1300 David Avenue is in the sub-area itself.

Parks, recreation and transit: Bert Flinn Park, the large forested park on the north shore, borders the Heritage Mountain grouping neighbourhoods; Heritage Mountain Community Centre is at 200 Panorama Place and Port Moody Public Library at 100 Newport Drive. TransLink buses serve the north shore and connect to Moody Centre Station and Coquitlam Central Station.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Heritage Woods

items.t: OCP — City of Port Moody Official Community Plan Bylaw 2026 No. 3522: (adopted April 28, 2026, repeals Bylaw No. 2955 — 2955 is never cited as current). Chapter 14, Section 14.3 covers Heritage Woods with the Heritage Mountain grouping (Heritage Mountain, Twin Creeks, Noons Creek, Mountain Meadows), with policies to retain the existing residential and forested character of the grouping.
Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 2937: single-detached homes sit in RS zones and multi-residential homes in RT and RM zones; minimum lot sizes are set zone by zone.
City stock is on municipal water and sewer, billed separately from taxes (2026 utility bill due February 27, 2026).

Port Moody property taxes: for 2026, due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on outstanding amounts after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 15, 2026; utilities are billed separately (2026 utility bill due February 27, 2026). This staged 5% + 5% is Port Moody's own municipal scheme as the City publishes it.

ALR position: For completeness only: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)) — check any parcel on the ALC maps if reserve status is ever in issue.

Strata block (applies to the sub-area's strata stock and in full to any bare-land strata lot): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF since November 1, 2023; rental bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

blocks.text: Good to know about Heritage Woods

items.t: A whole complex hides at 2000 Panorama Drive (Nov 2, 2026). It stays queued here, counted nowhere, until its sub-area filing is settled on a directory or developer source.
Cobalt Sky's published facts disagree with each other (Nov 1, 2026). Neither figure should be quoted in a listing — the strata plan BCS2068 and the Form B are the settlement documents.
Detached demand led Port Moody here in September 2026 — attached did not. (SnapStats, September 2026)

Both commute doors matter on this hillside (Nov 1, 2026). David Avenue runs east into Coquitlam as well as west into Port Moody, so Heritage Woods buyers working in either direction use the neighbourhood differently — and neither route involves a SkyTrain station in the sub-area itself.
The "Heritage Woods Senior Living" website is not a Port Moody residence (Nov 1, 2026).

blocks.text: Heritage Woods: streets and boundaries

items.t: Heritage Woods is the eastern part of Port Moody's Heritage Mountain grouping on the north shore, below Anmore and beside the Coquitlam border, centred on David Avenue east of Heritage Mountain Boulevard.

The City publishes no street-by-street boundary for Heritage Woods alone; the Official Community Plan (OCP) Bylaw No. 3522, Chapter 14, Section 14.3 treats it with Heritage Mountain, Twin Creeks, Noons Creek and Mountain Meadows.
Its house streets named on TransLink route 183 are Forest Park Way and Panorama Drive; David Avenue continues east into Coquitlam to Pinetree Way.

blocks.text: Heritage Woods: the housing stock

items.t: The landmark public building is Heritage Woods Secondary School at 1300 David Avenue, with North Shore Community Park's fields at the same address.
Aspenwood Elementary, 2001 Panorama Drive, and Aspenwood Park, 200 Panorama Place, sit inside the Panorama Drive loop on the neighbourhood's east side.

blocks.text: Heritage Woods: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Heritage Woods is outside the Inlet Centre and Moody Centre Transit-Oriented Areas, so the SSMUH position that applies here is the standard RS and RT zone position, not the transit-area exemption.
Environmentally sensitive and steep-slope development permit areas can apply on this hillside, and creek lots need a riparian assessment with Zoning Bylaw No. 2937 Section 5.4 setbacks.

blocks.text: Heritage Woods: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Dogs off leash outside the designated Bert Flinn trails can draw a ticket under Bylaw No. 3343; in all other Port Moody public spaces dogs must be on leash.
Heritage Mountain Community Centre is at 200 Panorama Place, inside Heritage Woods beside Aspenwood Park — despite carrying the Heritage Mountain name.
North Shore Community Park is listed at 1400 David Avenue for courts and 1300 David Avenue for a lit artificial turf field and a grass baseball and soccer field.
Port Moody Public Library is at 100 Newport Drive, south of the inlet.
David Avenue runs east into Coquitlam as well as west into Port Moody, so east-end homes use Coquitlam Central Station as readily as the Port Moody stations.

blocks.text: Heritage Woods: getting around

items.t: Route 183 is the Heritage Woods bus: Coquitlam Central Station via Panorama Drive, Forest Park Way, David Avenue at Heritage Woods Secondary and Heritage Mountain Boulevard to Moody Centre Station.

blocks.text: Heritage Woods: risks and due diligence

items.t: Hillside lots here can carry both environmentally sensitive and steep-slope development permit areas; both still apply to SSMUH units, so a coach house design needs the permit-area check first.

Homes backing onto the Bert Flinn Park forest are forest-interface lots; the City's hazards page notes Port Moody is surrounded by forests and parks and directs owners to FireSmart Canada for wildfire preparation.
Creek lots need a riparian assessment and Zoning Bylaw No. 2937 Section 5.4 setbacks confirmed before any addition is designed.

blocks.text: Heritage Woods home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

23 houses sold in Heritage Woods with a median price of $2,098,000 (the middle half sold between $1,872,500 and $2,265,000), taking a median of 18 days to sell at 96.8% of the last list price; 9% sold above list. They had a median $558 per square foot, a median year built of 2004 and a median lot of 6,515 square feet. 21 townhomes sold in Heritage Woods with a median price of $1,158,000 (the middle half sold between $997,000 and $1,280,000), taking a median of 16 days to sell at 98.3% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $631 per square foot, a median year built of 2004 and a median strata fee of $469 a month.

faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 23 houses and 6 condos and townhomes listed in Heritage Woods. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.
faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Heritage Woods?

faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 4% (a buyers’ market); condos and townhomes had 17% on only 6 listed, too few to read as a market type. The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.
faq.q: Is Heritage Woods a buyers’ or sellers’ market?

faq.a: 12 houses and 5 condos and townhomes sold in Heritage Woods over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in September with 4 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in June with 3 sold.
faq.q: How many homes sold in Heritage Woods from June to October 2026?

faq.a: In October 2026, Heritage Woods held 16.7% of the 138 detached houses listed in Port Moody and 3.6% of the 168 condos and townhomes listed in Port Moody.
faq.q: How big is Heritage Woods compared with the rest of Port Moody?

faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 79.3% of the 29 homes listed in Heritage Woods and condos and townhomes made up 20.7%; of the 2 that sold, houses were 50.0% and condos and townhomes 50.0%.
faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Heritage Woods?

faq.a: Listings of detached houses rose from 20 in June to 23 in October 2026 (+15.0%); condos and townhomes rose from 3 in June to 6 in October 2026 (+100.0%).
faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Heritage Woods than in June?

faq.a: Land trades here as individual fee-simple detached lots and resales inside the four counted townhouse strata.
faq.q: Is there a bare-land subdivision or lot program in Heritage Woods?

faq.a: They are built stock, not lot inventory.
faq.q: Which townhouse complexes are actually in Heritage Woods?

faq.a: An apartment buyer is, in practice, shopping Port Moody's apartment stock down the hill.
faq.q: Is there an apartment condo I can buy in Heritage Woods?

faq.a: Small-scale multi-unit housing, including coach houses and accessory dwelling units, is permitted on qualifying RS and RT lots outside the transit-oriented areas — up to four units on lots between 280 m² and 4,050 m², up to six within 400 m of frequent bus stops — and secondary suites are allowed in all single-detached residential zones; hillside lots may first trigger steep-slope or riparian permit requirements.
faq.q: Can I add a coach house or suites to a Heritage Woods lot under SSMUH?

faq.a: No. A coach house or ADU under Port Moody's SSMUH rules is part of the lot's single title — it adds rental or family flexibility to a purchase, never a separate purchase.
faq.q: Can I buy a coach house separately from the house?

faq.a: The permit areas: Steep slope and environmentally sensitive DP areas can apply, and creek lots need a riparian assessment with Section 5.4 setbacks — price that diligence before writing.
faq.q: What should a hillside buyer budget for?

faq.a: Yes. Heritage Woods Secondary, Grades 9 to 12, is at 1300 David Avenue inside Heritage Woods, and TransLink route 183 names its stop on David Avenue. Catchment still depends on the home address in School District No. 43 (SD43), so verify the exact house in the School Locator rather than assuming the nearest secondary school is the assigned one.
faq.q: Is Heritage Woods Secondary inside the neighbourhood?

faq.a: It depends on the address. The two catchments meet inside this area, so the street alone does not settle it.
faq.q: Aspenwood or Heritage Mountain elementary for my street?

faq.a: Eagle Mountain Middle, in Anmore, is the middle school returned for this catchment family. It sits outside Port Moody, north of David Avenue, so the middle-school trip crosses into the Village of Anmore within the same SD43. Buyers moving from a one-school city should confirm the middle and secondary pair for their exact address before subjects are removed.
faq.q: Where do students go for middle school?

faq.a: No station is in Heritage Woods. Route 183 runs from Coquitlam Central Station via Panorama Drive, Forest Park Way and David Avenue to Inlet Centre and Moody Centre stations, so the rail link is a bus ride east or west along David Avenue, not a walk. Plan the commute around the bus, and check the current 183 timetable for frequency.
faq.q: Can I walk to SkyTrain from Heritage Woods?
What did houses in Heritage Woods sell for?
faq.a: 23 houses sold in Heritage Woods between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $2,098,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Heritage Woods?
faq.a: The median was 18 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 96.8% of the last list price (9% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
